role: Software Engineer - Hardware Diagnostics - New Grad
have_skills: GPU & AI accelerator hardware (CUDA, TensorRT, Jetson, pynvml)
Peripheral driver code (UART, I2C, SPI, GPIO, PWM, ADC)
Cross-functional HW/mechanical collaboration (SolidWorks, PCB, robotics teams)
adjacent_skills: Distributed systems -> MPI + SLURM cluster parallelism
User-space driver/interface code -> Python/C sensor layers, ROS2 nodes
Hardware validation & diagnostics -> integration failure debug, scope/LA work
Custom test suites / test automation -> ad hoc benchmark + profiling harnesses
Stress & performance verification -> GPU/Jetson latency and VRAM profiling
Large-scale / datacenter deployment -> SLURM-managed cluster, JupyterHub
Platform software architecture -> custom RTOS scheduler, 3-layer pipeline design
missing_skills: Linux kernel-space driver development (kernel modules, device tree, ioctl, PCIe)
L2 networking protocols (Ethernet/MAC, VLAN, STP, LLDP)
Datacenter / server hardware domain (NICs, PCIe fabric, BMC/IPMI, power & thermal validation)
key_responsibilities: Design and write platform driver code across kernel and user space to model, stress, and verify hardware performance
Drive architectural decisions for platform software
Partner cross-functionally with hardware, software and mechanical teams to build custom test suites
End-to-end system enablement from prototype bring-up to large-scale AI datacenter deployment

strengths: Hard qualifications land squarely: Python across every internship, and real bare-metal C on Cortex-M4 programming GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1 registers directly (STM32 Temperature Monitor, 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM, deterministic 1 Hz).
Driver-level embedded work is genuine, not surface: low-level I2C driver, interrupt-driven UART, multi-servo PWM, FreeRTOS mutex task coordination (Object Tracking Turret, STM32 monitor).
Schematics/datasheets is backed by fabrication, not just reading: single-layer EAGLE PCBs for competition robots, plus datasheet-level sensor bring-up (VL53L0X, ADXL345, TCA9548A I2C mux).

The hardware/software boundary is the literal subject of the MS capstone: COFFIN spans Flutter client -> Flask-SocketIO server -> Jetson -> Arduino -> servos and ToF sensors over one WebSocket fabric.
Real hardware diagnostics narrative: resolved 11 integration failures including servo brown-out, stale-frame capture and false-positive detection, reaching 10/10 pick reliability.

'Model, stress, and verify hardware performance' has direct evidence: pynvml/psutil VRAM and latency profiling, CUDA coalesced-vs-uncoalesced kernel benchmarking (49.2ms vs 73.3ms), MPI load-imbalance characterization showing 65% degradation.
AI-accelerator context is a plus at an AI infra company: CUDA C++ kernels, TensorRT (5.2x YOLO speedup), Jetson deployment, 8-bit quantization.
real_gaps: No Linux kernel-space development anywhere: no kernel modules, char devices, ioctl, device tree, or PCIe drivers. All driver work is MCU register programming, which does not transfer directly.
No datacenter or server-class hardware: no NIC, PCIe fabric, BMC/IPMI/Redfish, rack power or thermal validation. Hardware experience tops out at dev boards and robotics.
No L2 networking at all (Ethernet/MAC, VLAN, STP, LLDP). Listed as a plus, but at an AI infrastructure company the fabric is central.
Distributed systems is thin: MPI and SLURM are HPC batch parallelism, not distributed systems as a discipline (RPC, consensus, fault tolerance, partial failure).
No formal test-suite engineering: benchmarking is ad hoc scripts, not pytest harnesses, regression suites or CI-driven validation frameworks.
Seniority note only (not scored here): 0 full-time years, but the role is explicitly New Grad with 1:1 mentorship, so this is not a real obstacle.
overstated_by_keywords: 'distributed systems' counted as adjacent via MPI/SLURM; a systems interviewer will find it thin
'driver code' counted as Have; bare-metal register writes are not Linux platform drivers
'datacenter deployment' counted as adjacent via a SLURM cluster, which is a very different scale
understated_by_keywords: The 11-integration-failure debug story is hardware diagnostics work and matches no keyword
Oscilloscopes and logic analyzers sit in the Tools list but never appear in a bullet, despite being a direct match for hardware validation
MPI load-imbalance characterization is performance verification under stress, which the keyword pass read only as HPC
screening_gaps: No Linux kernel-space driver development, while the first listed responsibility is platform driver code across kernel and user space
No datacenter or server hardware exposure (PCIe, NICs, BMC, power/thermal); hardware experience is dev-board and robotics scale
No L2 networking knowledge, which is load-bearing at an AI infrastructure company even though the JD marks it a plus
llm_analysis.reasoning: The stated qualifications, which are what actually gate a new-grad screen, are met almost fully: Python, C, embedded systems, schematics and datasheets are all backed by hands-on work, and the capstone is a real hardware/software bring-up and debug story. The gaps are in kernel-space drivers, datacenter hardware and L2 networking, which are genuine but are exactly the things a New Grad role with 1:1 mentorship expects to teach. Apply, and lead with bare-metal driver work and hardware debug rather than the ML projects.
